newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Rains, shortcovering to shore up prices.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Rains, shortcovering to shore up prices.

text.p: Rains in Malaysia and Thailand and light shortcovering in Indonesia should keep rubber prices firm this week, but the the market is expected to drift ahead of the Christmas holiday period, regional traders said on Monday.
"There are signs of more buying interest, mostly from Singapore, but any rises are likely to be limited as this interest is only for shortcovering," a dealer in SIR20 rubber in Indonesia said.

"Normally, the rains in Malaysia and Thailand would have sent prices shooting up. But there are no orders and you have a very thin market. I also don't think this shortcovering will run much longer especially with Christmas around the corner," a dealer for a Japanese rubber trading firm in Singapore said.

Malaysian traders said producers were inclined to demand higher prices although the market was virtually dead because seasonal rains have hampered tapping at plantations and reduced the supply of latex and other materials into the market.
"Almost all overseas consumers and buyers are on holiday and I don't see any reason for fresh demand next week," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur. "This is solely on supply sentiment."

"You'll continue to see shortcovering this week, but it will probably begin to tail off by Friday and buying will not probably come back until after the New Year," a dealer for a U.S. rubber trading firm said.
Another Indonesian dealer said demand for shoe-grade SIR3CV was also rising as firms expected an increase in demand for shoes because of the holiday season.

"Demand is seen rising for SIR3CV. In the first two weeks of December alone we have secured deals worth 350 tonnes of SIR3CV, up from a monthly average of 300 this year," the Medan-based SIR3CV dealer said.
The dealer said he expected the SIR3CV to go up to around 145.00 U.S. cents/kg from the current 142 cents on higher demand.

Indonesian dealers said February/March SIR20 offer prices were at 55.00-55.50 cents/lb FOB Medan, 54.75-55.25 FOB Surabaya, Padang and Palembang, 54.00-54.50 FOB Pontianak and Jambi, unchanged from the previous week.
In Kuala Lumpur, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the January benchmark RSS1 rubber at Malaysian 317 cents a kg. January SMR20 buyer was quoted at 308.50 cents.
Dealers said they expected the two grades to move up three to five cents this week. Latex was offered by trading houses in Kuala Lumpur at 237 cents a kg last week.
Heavy monsoon rains also pinched supplies in Thailand's rubber producing areas and combined with Japanese buying to push prices up last week in a trend that may persist this week, traders said.
"It seemed that Japan entered the market to buy the product before the holiday season," one Bangkok-based trader said.
But the buying was limited because the quality of the sheet rubber was being affected by the heavy rains.
"Japanese buyers are very picky on quality. Heavy rains at the moment raised moisture content and contamination in the (rubber) sheets," said one trader in Hat Yai.
The benchmark RSS3 for January shipment was quoted around US$1.24-1.25 a kg FOB Bangkok compared with around $1.23-1.24.
February deliveries also edged up to $1.24-$1.25 a kg from $1.24 and latex rose to $0.94 a kg from $0.93.
But demand for STR20 rubber for January shipment was thin as China, its traditional buyer, was absent.
(With contributions from Anchalee Koetsawang in Thailand, K.T. Arasu in Indonesia and Barani Krishnaan in Malaysia)
-- Singapore Newsroom 65-8703305)
